label: The built state's hook cost is p50 189 ms, p95 290 ms, p99 300 ms, max 2,218 ms over 17,775 persisted health records from 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-16; seven rows exceed 1,000 ms and three exceed 2,000 ms.
Per-day hook p95 is flat at 290-291 ms from 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-15 while the daily max rose from 922 to 2,218 ms; the 2026-11-16 partial day reads p50 136 and p95 212 over 580 rows.
No measured hook row exceeded the Claude 2,500 ms budget, but the 2,218 ms maximum used 88.7 percent of it and leaves 282 ms of headroom.

The duration distribution has a hard cliff at 300 ms: 4,674 rows spread almost uniformly across 240-299 ms at about 778 per 10 ms bin, then only 87 rows beyond 300 ms, so p95 290 ms measures a cut rather than the work.

The shim reserves CHILD_START_MARGIN_MS = 300 after the advisor CLI and the hook stamps durationMs at the brief result, but which component stops at 300 ms is not proven by the record; a trace of one prompt crossing the boundary would confirm it.
One brief costs 270.7 bytes on average and 361 bytes at most over 1,138 emitting rows on the built state, about 68 tokens at the renderer's four-characters-per-token estimate.

No byte remains removable from a brief without reversing a swept decision: the head and companion share a 320-character cap and the 219-byte comment-hygiene directive is appended after that cap as a repo hard block.

The committed arm caps 47 turns, not the 41 in the dispatch brief: opencode 26, devin 19, pi 2, claude 0, dsh 0 across 400 runs; the raw census reads 28 exit-143 rows and 20 nulls, of which one null is the fresh-skill-04 rebase row.

The turn cap is keyed to the prompt kind (300,000 ms chat, 900,000 ms started) and the runner records only an exit code, so a null exit conflates a cap kill with a spawn error and no elapsed time is stored.
The phase 033 OpenCode arena sessions survive in none of the five local OpenCode databases, so no message timestamp can measure how long a capped turn ran.
The arenas were built at b765c7a14c5, six documentation-only commits before HEAD 84de3d600fa, so the arm's behaviour numbers describe that build and no hook-time code changed after it.
